newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WINS TOSS, PUTS WEST INDIES IN TO BAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WINS TOSS, PUTS WEST INDIES IN TO BAT.

text.p: Pakistan captain Wasim Akram won the toss and sent West Indies in to bat in a World Series limited overs match at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Tuesday.
Both teams rested key players and gave second-line players a chance in the match, which is irrelevant to the make-up of the best-of-three finals series series starting at the weekend.
Pakistan and West Indies have already made the finals, with host nation Australia eliminated from the annual tri-nation competition for the first time since the 1979/80 season.
West Indies rested left-handed batting star Brian Lara, who had scored 295 runs in West Indies' past three matches.
Regular West Indies captain Courtney Walsh stood down for the match, handing the captaincy to middle-order batsman Carl Hooper.

The major interest in the Pakistan team will focus on the performances of fast bowler Waqar Younis, who has had a long break with a shoulder injury, and batsman Inzamam-ul-Haq, who was dropped for Pakistan's previous match against West Indies.
West Indies successfully chased Pakistan's 257 for seven in that match in Perth last Friday, a factor which no doubt influenced Pakistan captain Wasim Akram's decision to ask West Indies to bat.
West Indies have won their last five limited overs matches in a row and lead the series on 10 points from Pakistan on six.

West Indies - Sherwin Campbell, Junior Murray, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Adrian Griffith, Robert Samuels, Carl Hooper (captain), Jimmy Adams, Roland Holder, Nixon McLean, Ian Bishop, Patterson Thompson.
Pakistan - Aamir Sohail, Zahoor Elahi, Ijaz Ahmed, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Mujahid Jamshed, Ijaz Ahmed Junior, Moin Khan, Wasim Akram (captain), Saqlain Mushtaq, Mushtaq Ahmed, Waqar Younis.
